Chinchero is situated in the Sacred Valley of the Incas near Cusco. The settlement is known for its traditional crafts and archaeological heritage. Foundations and remains of the palace of the Inca Túpac Yupanqui have survived here, with colonial buildings later constructed above them. This juxtaposition reveals several periods in the history of a single place.

Chinchero's living culture is especially evident in the work of local artisans and at the Sunday market. Handmade goods showcase techniques and patterns that local people still use today. A visit to Chinchero adds another dimension to exploring the towns of the Sacred Valley: historical structures stand alongside the everyday life of a community of craftspeople.

Chivay is a gateway for journeys to Colca Canyon. The town offers a place to stop in the mountains before travelling to the viewpoints. Its surroundings reveal an Andean landscape very different from coastal Lima and Peru's larger cities.

There are hot springs nearby where travellers can unwind after a day on the road or exploring nature. From Chivay, the route continues towards Cruz del Cóndor and other points along the canyon. The town adds a chance to discover a small settlement in the Colca Valley to a journey of condor-watching and mountain panoramas.

Cholula is known as a major urban centre of the pre-Columbian era. The Great Pyramid of Cholula is an important part of the history of religious life in ancient Mexico. The city lies in the region of the Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl volcanoes, which shape the mountainous setting of this part of the country.

A visit to Cholula complements walks around Puebla with an introduction to the region's earlier monuments. The meeting of the ancient complex and the modern city is particularly striking, as are its streets and local traditions. Cholula shows how pre-Columbian history remains part of the everyday urban landscape.

Choroní lies on Venezuela's Caribbean coast, at the foot of the forested slopes of Henri Pittier National Park. The settlement's historic buildings and fishing traditions sit alongside tropical rainforest and the sea. The road to the coast passes through mountainous terrain.

A stay in Choroní combines strolls through the settlement with time on the beaches. Nearby bays and natural areas offer opportunities for trips along the shore and out onto the sea. The area makes an appealing introduction to coastal Venezuela after time spent in Caracas.

Chorro del Macho is located in the El Valle de Antón area. Forest surrounds the waterfall, while trails and hanging walkways allow visitors to explore its natural setting. The falling water adds a distinct riverside scene to the valley's mountain landscapes.

A visit can be combined with walks around El Valle and other natural attractions nearby. The cascade itself, the plants growing beside the water and the forested stretches along the way are all worth seeing. Chorro del Macho offers a peaceful stop surrounded by greenery after exploring the local market and the village set in a volcanic valley.
